questions.question: What is 'tie capacity'? The source says it is the 'rated capacity' (a static nameplate rating) but also says it arrives from the SCADA scan every 10 s (a live value, usually the alternate feeder's spare capacity). Which is it, and in which unit: kW (what the code uses today), kVA or A (feeders carry rating_amps)? If it is kVA or A, what power factor or voltage converts the load_kw load basis, and what p.u. base should the tolerance use?
When is a 10 s scan value 'late' (for example 20 s = 2 missed scans, or 30 s)? Inside that window, may the planner hold the last good value, or must it refuse any value older than one scan?

Today tie_capacity_kw is a bare dict[str, float] with no timestamp or quality. How should the value's timestamp and SCADA quality reach build_plan and POST /flisr/plan? May we extend the build_plan signature and the POST /flisr/plan body (an API change for the SCADA adapter), and who owns the adapter side?
When transferred load exactly equals tie capacity, should the tie close or not? Is a safety margin or comparison tolerance needed, stated in kW and p.u.?

The source says 'the plan must say so instead of restoring'. When one tie's capacity is unknown, is only that tie blocked (the lockout reclose and ties with known capacity still go ahead), or is the whole restoration refused (isolation-only / manual-action plan, or HTTP 409)? Must 'capacity unknown' also be a machine-readable RestorationPlan field, not only a free-text note?
When load exceeds capacity, should the planner try a partial pick-up (open a downstream sectionalizer so the rest fits), or is skipping the tie the required outcome? Skipping is today's behaviour.

When two or more ties pick up load from the same alternate feeder, is capacity per tie, or shared so that the sum of the transfers must fit? The shipped model has one tie, so the source does not settle this.

The brief's layer map names backend/app/state_estimation.py and backend/app/main.py, but those files do not exist; the real files are state_estimator.py and api.py. The source also names locate_fault as the planner, but the capacity logic is in build_plan. Please confirm that build_plan plus api.py is the intended scope, and correct the repo contract's layer map.

summary: The specification is drafted and saved as artifacts.specification. It has 9 requirements (REQ-FLISR-001..009), 3 defects reproduced on main@5f6b471 (DEF-FLISR-001..003), the safety invariant INV-1, a verification method and independent BFS oracle for each requirement, and a scope-exclusion list. The verdict is BLOCKED because 8 questions are open (Q-SPEC-1..8): the capacity quantity and unit, the staleness limit and hold-last-value window, how timestamp and quality are delivered, behaviour at equality, per-tie vs whole-plan refusal, partial pick-up, shared capacity, and file-name errors in the repo contract. Probing build_plan found that today a NaN capacity closes TIE-1201-1405 and transfers 1490 kW; +inf also restores; and a missing capacity is silently treated as 0 kW, which closes the tie when the candidate load is 0 kW. No code was changed, so no branch, commit or PR was created.

answer: Live value. 'Tie capacity' is the alternate feeder's spare capacity as delivered by the SCADA scan every 10 s, in kW on the same basis as load_kw. No unit conversion, no p.u. base; comparison tolerance is 0.5 kW. The 'rated capacity' wording in the source is loose and does not mean nameplate.

A value is late when it is older than 20 s (two missed scans). Inside 20 s the planner may use the last value only if its quality is GOOD. Older than 20 s, or any quality other than GOOD, is 'unknown' and must not be used.

Extend build_plan with tie_capacity: dict[str, TieCapacity] where TieCapacity carries kw, timestamp and quality (a Pydantic model in backend/app/models.py). Extend the POST /flisr/plan body the same way. Keep the legacy dict[str, float] accepted for one release and treat it as quality GOOD with timestamp now, with a deprecation note. The SCADA adapter side is owned by the integration team and is out of scope for this change.
Equality closes: the tie may close when transferred load <= capacity. No additional safety margin; the only tolerance is the 0.5 kW comparison tolerance from Q-SPEC-1. No p.u. statement needed.

Per tie. Only the tie with unknown capacity is blocked; isolation and ties with a known capacity proceed. 'Capacity unknown' must be machine-readable: RestorationPlan gains blocked_ties: list[BlockedTie{tie_id, reason in CAPACITY_UNKNOWN | CAPACITY_STALE | CAPACITY_INVALID | CAPACITY_EXCEEDED}] and an operator-readable note; HTTP 200, not 409.
Skip the tie (today's behaviour) and record it in blocked_ties with reason CAPACITY_EXCEEDED. Partial pick-up is out of scope.
Per tie. Shared alternate-feeder capacity across several ties is out of scope; list it as a scope exclusion.
Confirmed: scope is build_plan in backend/app/flisr.py plus backend/app/api.py (and models.py for the new types). The repo contract layer map has been corrected to state_estimator.py / api.py.

questions.question: What triggers CAPACITY_INVALID, and how are reasons assigned? (a) Which kw values are invalid: NaN, ±inf, negative? A negative spare capacity could be a real reading (alternate feeder already overloaded) or a bad value; with L=0 kW and C=-0.3 the tie would close unless negative values are invalid. (b) Does quality != GOOD give CAPACITY_UNKNOWN or CAPACITY_INVALID? (c) BlockedTie has one reason: when several conditions hold (e.g. stale + not GOOD + NaN), which is recorded? (d) A malformed HTTP entry (e.g. string kw, missing quality): reject the whole request with 422, or block only that tie with CAPACITY_INVALID and return 200?

What is the time reference for staleness? (a) Is t_eval the planner's UTC wall clock when build_plan starts, or an evaluation time supplied by the caller or injected? (b) A timestamp later than t_eval (clock skew): usable, stale, or invalid? Is any skew allowed? Without a rule a future-dated value looks fresh indefinitely. (c) A timezone-naive timestamp: reject, or interpret as UTC?

How does the legacy dict[str, float] coexist with the new form? (a) HTTP body: keep the legacy floats under tie_capacity_kw next to a new tie_capacity field, or one field that accepts either shape? (b) If both forms are supplied in one call, or for the same tie: refuse, new form wins, or something else? (c) Where does the 'deprecation note' go: RestorationPlan.notes (shown to operators), an HTTP Deprecation header, OpenAPI deprecated, a log line, or several?

Three gaps remain that the source and Q-SPEC-1..8 do not settle: Q-SPEC-9 (what counts as CAPACITY_INVALID, which reason a non-GOOD quality gets, precedence between reasons, malformed HTTP input), Q-SPEC-10 (time reference, future-dated and timezone-naive timestamps) and Q-SPEC-11 (how the legacy and new body forms coexist, and where the deprecation note goes). answer: CAPACITY_INVALID = kw is NaN, +/-inf, negative, or not a finite number, or the timestamp is unparseable/timezone-naive/future-dated (see Q-SPEC-10). A quality other than GOOD is CAPACITY_UNKNOWN (same as missing). Precedence when several apply, evaluate in this order and report the first: CAPACITY_INVALID, CAPACITY_UNKNOWN, CAPACITY_STALE, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED. Malformed HTTP input (wrong types, unknown fields) is rejected by request validation with HTTP 422 and never reaches the planner.

Time reference is the request's as_of field: a timezone-aware ISO-8601 UTC instant supplied by the caller; when absent the server uses UTC now and echoes the value it used in the response. Capacity timestamps must be timezone-aware; naive timestamps are CAPACITY_INVALID. A timestamp more than 2 s ahead of as_of is CAPACITY_INVALID. Age = as_of - timestamp.

The new body field tie_capacity (dict[str, TieCapacity]) and the legacy tie_capacity_kw are mutually exclusive; both present is HTTP 422. Legacy-only requests are treated as quality GOOD with timestamp = as_of and the response carries deprecations: ['tie_capacity_kw']. The deprecation note lives in the endpoint's OpenAPI description and in the docs page the Document stage produces; removal is a separate change after one release.

questions.question: Invalid as_of. Q-SPEC-10 only covers a missing as_of. What happens when the supplied as_of is (a) timezone-naive, (b) aware but with a non-UTC offset such as +02:00 (accept it as the same instant, or reject?), or (c) unparseable? The two options are: reject with HTTP 422, so no plan and not even isolation; or build the plan with isolation and block every candidate tie as CAPACITY_INVALID. (d) Should a supplied as_of be bounded against the server clock? Without a bound, a caller can back-date as_of so that stale capacity looks fresh, which bypasses the 20 s staleness rule.

Unparseable capacity timestamp over HTTP. Q-SPEC-9 says an unparseable timestamp is CAPACITY_INVALID (per tie, HTTP 200) and that wrong types get HTTP 422 for the whole request. In JSON the timestamp is a string either way, so is a non-ISO-8601 string such as 'yesterday' (a) a per-tie CAPACITY_INVALID with HTTP 200, which means TieCapacity.timestamp must accept any string, or (b) a 422? And is a JSON number (Unix seconds) a wrong type (422) or accepted?

summary: SPECIFY attempt 3. prepare: STD-GOV, STD-REQ and STD-SAFETY loaded; read .agents/skills/safety-critical-change/SKILL.md, DEMO_NOTES.md, flisr.py, api.py, models.py and network.py; re-measured the baseline on main@5f6b471. execute: applied Q-SPEC-9..11 and wrote 22 requirements (REQ-TIECAP-1..22), each with its missing/late/invalid behaviour, a verification method and an independent oracle, plus scope exclusions and blast radius. New finding: on main today a NaN or +inf tie capacity CLOSES TIE-1201-1405 (L > NaN is False). The HTTP layer accepts JSON NaN, turns "2000" into a number and ignores unknown fields. verify: re-checked every requirement against STD-REQ-1..7, STD-SAFETY-2/4/5/6/7 and STD-GOV-1/2/6/7. deliver: BLOCKED on two new gaps the answers do not cover. Q-SPEC-12: a supplied as_of that is invalid (naive, non-UTC, unparseable) or back-dated against the server clock. Q-SPEC-13: whether an unparseable capacity timestamp over HTTP is a 422 or a per-tie CAPACITY_INVALID. Only REQ-TIECAP-1, -2, -8 and -13 depend on them. Spec pushed to agent/feature-tie-capacity/specify (d9e1605); no PR opened, matching the earlier attempts.

answer: (a) timezone-naive as_of: HTTP 422. (b) aware non-UTC offset: accept, normalise to the same UTC instant. (c) unparseable: HTTP 422. (d) yes, bounded: an as_of more than 60 s before or 2 s after the server clock is HTTP 422, so staleness cannot be bypassed by back-dating. 422 means no plan at all, which is acceptable because the request itself is malformed; the operator retries with a valid request.

(b) 422. TieCapacity.timestamp is a strict timezone-aware ISO-8601 datetime field; a non-ISO string or a JSON number is a request-validation failure for the whole request. Per-tie CAPACITY_INVALID for timestamps therefore covers only well-formed values that fail the semantic rules (future-dated beyond 2 s). Q-SPEC-9 is amended to match.

Which rule governs the QA oracle? (a) STD-SAFETY-6 (proposed): the oracle restates the closed form with literals from the spec, and one test pins the models.py constants to the spec values; STD-ARCH-2 then applies only to production consumers. (c) Middle ground: the oracle imports the models.py constants only and restates the comparison and the precedence.

questions.question: A section with negative Section.load_kw (e.g. DG export) inside a candidate set whose total L is still >= 0 makes L understate the load the tie would actually carry (measured: spur -600 kW, C=1000 -> closes at L=890 kW while the non-negative loads total 1490 kW). Pick one: (a) refuse the plan with FlisrError when any candidate-section load_kw < 0 (recommended; REQ-TIECAP-3/21 scoped to non-negative section loads); (b) use gross L = sum(max(load_kw, 0)) (changes the spec's L definition); (c) keep REQ-TIECAP-3 literal and accept the residual risk; (d) declare negative loads out of scope (model-team rule, no runtime check).

Draft PR #13 (DEF-FLISR-7) holds a candidate tie open with a note and no blocked_ties entry, which contradicts REQ-TIECAP-21 ('every candidate tie not closed appears exactly once in blocked_ties'). Pick one: (a) ties held open by the DEF-FLISR-7 guard are not candidate ties for REQ-TIECAP-11/18/21; the guard runs before L and the verdict (recommended); (b) add a fifth BlockedTie reason, e.g. BACKFEED_FAULTED_SECTION, ahead of CAPACITY_INVALID (changes Q-SPEC-5 enum, REQ-TIECAP-9/11); (c) fix a merge order and let the second change amend its own requirements.

summary: Design attempt 3 (commit 43ccfa2 on agent/feature-tie-capacity/design). Architect finding A-1 (STD-ARCH-4) is resolved within the spec's range L >= 0: tie_capacity_verdict states and enforces preconditions (ValueError) for L NaN/±inf/<0, a naive or non-datetime as_of, a naive entry.timestamp and an entry of the wrong type, and build_plan raises FlisrError (no plan, HTTP 409) for an out-of-range L. Measured on main: a NaN, -inf or -120 kW section load closes the tie today. O-2..O-4 are addressed, O-1 and O-5 accepted, and the STD-SAFETY-7 tool-classification argument is added. The design is BLOCKED on two gaps that resolving A-1 turned up, each needing a departure from REQ-TIECAP-3/21: Q-DESIGN-2 (a negative section load inside a non-negative L understates the transfer, measured close at 890 kW vs 1490 kW gross) and Q-DESIGN-3 (the DEF-FLISR-7 hold-open guard on draft PR #13 contradicts REQ-TIECAP-21). The four phases: prepare (STD-ARCH, STD-GOV, STD-SAFETY loaded; SKILL.md and DEMO_NOTES.md read), execute (design edited), verify (§8 re-checked clause by clause; 23/23 REQ ids mapped; pytest 2 passed; ruff clean), deliver (this verdict).

answer: A negative, NaN or infinite section load is invalid model data, not a load to net off. build_plan refuses the whole plan (FlisrError, HTTP 409, lockout stays open) when any candidate section's load_kw is not a finite non-negative number; L is otherwise the plain sum. This is covered by the out-of-range precondition and needs no change to REQ-TIECAP-3/21; record it in the design as a stated precondition and add a test vector.

Draft PR #13 (DEF-FLISR-7 hold-open guard) lands first and is kept. Design on top of it: a tie refused because its pick-up set touches the faulted section is reported in blocked_ties with a new reason FAULTED_SECTION, evaluated before every capacity reason (precedence FAULTED_SECTION > CAPACITY_INVALID > CAPACITY_UNKNOWN > CAPACITY_STALE > CAPACITY_EXCEEDED). REQ-TIECAP-21 is amended accordingly in the spec by the Design stage (note the amendment in design.md and the trace); the guard's behaviour must not change.
